predecessors.name: Akkadian Empire
predecessors.text: Adab from the end of the Akkadian period, the Sumerian plain from 2189, 'northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish' at the dynasty's end in 2154

successors.name: Uruk
successors.text: Sumer, 'both banks of the Tigris', to Utu-hengal who 'established himself as the king of Sumer'

ledger.x: 2220 BCE: Erridupizir, king of Gutium, holds Adab.
2189 BCE: the Gutians take the Sumerian plain as Akkad shrinks.
2154 BCE: the Akkadian dynasty ends and Akkad passes to the Gutians.
2119 BCE: Utu-hengal of Uruk defeats Tirigan.

wars.name: Utu-hengal's war against Tirigan
wars.outcome: Tirigan captured, 'the kingship of the land of Sumer' passed to Uruk; Ur-Nammu of Ur followed within seven years.

certainty.note: Nothing is surveyed: the Gutian homeland is unknown, the Mesopotamian holdings are known from a capital (Adab), governors (Umma) and a river ('both banks of the Tigris'); every edge is bridged.
